# v2.71-dev — the non-root upgrade now completes itself

A follow-up to v2.70-dev, which moved the application off root. That release needed one manual command on the server to finish the job. This one removes that requirement for most installs and makes the requirement impossible to miss for the rest.

> ### ⚠️ Upgrading from v2.69 or earlier — please read
>
> **If you have automatic updates switched on**, there is nothing to do. Within about five minutes of updating, the server finishes the migration on its own: it creates the service account, corrects file ownership, installs the update helper, and restarts the app so it comes back unprivileged. You will see this in `/var/log/training-tracker/updates.log`.
>
> **If you do not have automatic updates switched on**, run this once on the server after updating:
>
> ```bash
> bash /opt/training-tracker/deploy/install.sh
> ```
>
> Run it **as root**. On an LXC you are normally root already; on a VM, prefix it with `sudo`.
>
> Until one of those two things happens, **the in-app "Update now" button will refuse to run** — it returns an error telling you exactly this — and the app keeps running as root, so you get none of the security benefit. The script is safe to re-run and leaves your database and settings untouched.
>
> The reason any of this is needed: the updater performing a v2.69 → v2.70 upgrade *is v2.69's updater*. It knows nothing about service accounts, so it cannot set one up while installing the release that introduces them. Once you are on v2.70 or later, every update applies its own changes and this never arises again.

## What changed

**The migration finishes itself.** The scheduled-update job runs as root every few minutes, which makes it the natural place to complete an upgrade the previous release could not. It now checks whether the service account and update helper are in place and, if not, sets them up and restarts the app unprivileged. The check is deliberately cheap so it costs nothing on the vast majority of ticks where there is nothing to do.

**Scheduled jobs are no longer defined in two places.** The installer and the updater now share one definition, so an update can add or correct a scheduled job instead of leaving whatever the original install wrote.

**Leftover scheduled jobs from before v2.70 are cleaned up.** Older versions had the app write its own update and export jobs into the system scheduler. Those are now standard system entries, so the superseded copies are removed during migration — without this, report exports would have been triggered twice a minute. Your **backup** schedule is deliberately left alone so that backups cannot be silently switched off; it continues to work as before.

## Notes

- The v2.70-dev release notes have been updated to flag the manual step as a breaking change. It was described there, but not marked clearly enough to be noticed.
